title: What will be the highest intraday value of the VIX between October 1 and December 24, 2026?
resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as the highest "High" value of ^VIX for any date between October 1, 2026, and December 24, 2026 (inclusive), according to [Yahoo! Finance](https://au.finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EVIX/history/).

For example, in the month of August 2026, the highest intraday value for ^VIX was 18.43 (on August 5).
fine_print: If the Yahoo Finance data is found to be unreliable, alternative sources such as the [CBOE VIX Index](https://www.cboe.com/tradable-products/vix/vix-historical-data) may be used instead. However, any revisions to the data after December 24, 2026 will not count toward resolution.
background:
Per [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VIX):

> VIX is the [ticker symbol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ticker_symbol "Ticker symbol") and popular name for the [Chicago Board Options Exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Board_Options_Exchange "Chicago Board Options Exchange")'s CBOE Volatility Index, a popular measure of the [stock market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stock_market "Stock market")'s expectation of [volatility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volatility_\(finance\) "Volatility (finance)") based on [S\&P 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S\&P_500 "S\&P 500") index [options](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Option_\(finance\) "Option (finance)"). It is calculated and disseminated on a real-time basis by the CBOE, and is often referred to as the *fear index* or *fear gauge*.

comments.author: DeRuina
comments.text: One thing I think is easy to miss here: the VIX futures curve (Oct \~18, Nov \~19, Dec \~19-20) prices the expected level, not the maximum. This question resolves on the window's single highest intraday print, and that almost always lands well above where futures sit. Looking at FRED closes for Oct 1 to Dec 24 over 2010-2025, the peak close beat 20 in 13 of 16 years and beat 25 in 10. Intraday highs typically add another point or more. The only sub-20 peaks came in calm regimes like 2012, 2013, and 2017, and 2026 has already printed 35 in March with a Fed hiking into an oil shock. I also can't find a recent year where the VIX spiked above 30 earlier in the year and then stayed under 20 for the whole of Q4 — 2010 (48 in May) still peaked around 23.5 in Q4, and 2015 (53 in August) around 26. Anchoring near the futures curve seems too low to me. What I'm watching: whether the VIX can stay under 18 through the Oct 21 expiry, which would be the first real sign this year's regime has actually shifted. Anyone have a counterexample to the "spike year, calm Q4" pattern?

comments.author: Theomachado
comments.text: ## **For this question, I approach it the following way:** 1 - VIX historical (outside view) 2 - The derivatives stack. VIX futures and options (outside view) 3 - Data on news-based geopolitical risk, rates, oil, and credit to see which actually predict the window max, then apply only the ones that survived. (inside view) 4 - Second-order catalyst: the Iran war picking up hard, with forecasts based on prediction markets. *** ### **Resolution criteria** Very much what we are already adapted to with MP comps, but the forecast is 60 trading days out, not just 10. *** ### **Where VIX is, and why this autumn is not a normal low-vol autumn** * **Low level, loud backdrop.** * VIX is at 16 even with a live war: Hormuz has been largely shut since the war began on Feb 28, and the US blockade was reinstated Jul 15. * Oil is about \$95 WTI and about \$99 Brent. * The Fed, under Warsh, hiked on Sep 16, its first hike in three years. * The 10-year yield is around 5.2%, the highest since 2007. This is very different from what we saw in the first half of the year, when the VIX was expected to be much higher given the macroeconomic scenario. It seems that the markets are adapting to this high volatility and not too much "desperate" **2026 monthly intraday maxima:** Jan 21.0, Feb 23.1, **Mar 35.3** (war shock), Apr 28.0, May 19.4, Jun 23.3, Jul 20.9, Aug 18.4, Sep 18.9. (The September high came on the day of the FOMC hike. Which was already very much priced in) **Calendar on what can drive the VIX:** *** ## **My read and catalysts:** ### **Outside view, part 1: VIX's own history** | Component | Median | P(>30) | P(>40) | Blend weight | | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ | ------ | ------ | ------------ | | A. Empirical 60-day windows from VIX 14.5–18, 1992–2026 (day-weighted) | 23.2 | 22% | 7% | 35% | | B. Oct 1 – Dec 24 windows with Sep close \< 19 (19 years) | 22.5 | 11% | 5% | 10% | | C. HAR(1,5,22) log-VIX + GJR-GARCH(t), with (z, high-excess) pairs bootstrapped from 2004–2026 | 23.6 | 26% | 13% | 30% | | D. C calibrated to the VIX option smiles (drift +0.001/day, shocks ×1.2) | 25.8 | 36% | 19% | — | | D, haircut by k \= 0.8 on log-excess to remove the vol risk premium | 23.5 | 25% | 12% | 25% | | Outside blend | 23.3 | 23% | 10% | | Each dot is one year since 1992: the September VIX close against the highest intraday VIX between Oct 1 and Dec 24, with midterm years in orange and the y-axis on a log scale, so equal vertical distances mean equal percentage moves. My takeaways from catalyst 1. * **Midterm years don't add much.** Their autumn peak median is 1.15× the September close, versus 1.33× in other years. The exceptions were big, though: 2018 went from 12.1 to 36.1. * **The main cluster sits at 20–30, which is already priced in.** *** ### **Outside view, part 2: the derivatives stack** * Options pay for a fatter tail than history supports. VIX options imply 32% above 30 and 16% above 40, while the history-based model gives 23% and 10%. The gap is the usual premium buyers pay for protection. * The forecast follows history, nudged up. It sits on the historical curve and adds a little in the 25–35 range for elevated hedging demand and war risk (26% above 30, 10% above 40), without paying the options' full premium. *** ### **Inside view 1 &2: alternative data and the war catalyst** Which signals actually predict the max? I ran a regression with data from 2009 to today to better understand the movements. * **The loud macro story doesn't.** Geopolitical-risk news, the 10-year yield jump, oil, and credit are all extreme today (+1.6 to +2.0 sd). None of them predicts a bigger max once you know where VIX is, because the VIX level already prices them. ***The war catalyst prices a new escalation, not the current level.*** * **War reaches VIX through oil.** Over 1992–2026, geopolitical-risk news and VIX are basically uncorrelated (−0.07). In 2026, the VIX–oil daily correlation flipped to about +0.5, and on days when oil rose 5% or more, VIX rose a median of 10%. * **Most escalations are noise.** * Major strike exchanges pushed it to 1.26× the pre-event close, and 2026 flare-ups to 1.27×. * **The market is exhausted of pricing in the Trump threats, and now the VIX doesn't move as much with the new tweets. Just like the classic fable of "The Shepherd Boy & the Wolf"** * Inside this war, the market has grown used to it: the peak after each flare-up fell from 35.3 to 28.0, then 20.3, then 18.9. | | | | | | | | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ---- | --- | --- | | No hard escalation | US strike on Iran 63% (routine for this war) | 78% | 23.5 | 23% | 10% | | Air-war escalation | Polymarket: Iran airspace closed 22%, Israeli airspace closed 18%, Bab el-Mandeb closed 18% | 13% | 25.2 | 25% | 10% | | Energy shock | WTI above its \$147 record 9.5% (Polymarket), oil at \$150 11% (Manifold), US ground invasion 3.9% (Metaculus) | 9% | 30.3 | 52% | 14% | * **Strikes are routine now; big escalation is a real but minority risk.** * **Only the energy-shock tier moves VIX a lot.** Markets agree on about 9–11% for oil at a record, or \$150. That scenario pushes the window max to around 30, while an air war alone barely lifts it above the no-escalation case. **In short:** history puts the Oct–Dec peak at 22–24 given today's 16, and options, dealer positioning, and hedging demand fatten the tail. A 22% chance of hard war escalation adds weight around 27–30, but only an oil shock gets to 35+, so I land on a median of 24, with 18% above 30 and 8% above 40. Hope this research help in y’all forecasts. *** ## **Sources:** * [https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EVIX/history/](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EVIX/history/) * [https://cdn.cboe.com/api/global/us\_indices/daily\_prices/VIX\_History.csv](https://cdn.cboe.com/api/global/us_indices/daily_prices/VIX_History.csv) * [https://www.cboe.com/delayed\_quotes/vix/quote\_table](https://www.cboe.com/delayed_quotes/vix/quote_table) * [https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm) * [https://polymarket.com/event/us-iran-ceasefire-continues-throughptptpt](https://polymarket.com/event/us-iran-ceasefire-continues-throughptptpt) * [https://polymarket.com/event/iran-full-airspace-closure-byptptpt-20260625195253028](https://polymarket.com/event/iran-full-airspace-closure-byptptpt-20260625195253028) * [https://polymarket.com/event/israeli-airspace-closed-by](https://polymarket.com/event/israeli-airspace-closed-by) * [https://polymarket.com/event/crude-oil-all-time-high-by](https://polymarket.com/event/crude-oil-all-time-high-by) * [https://manifold.markets/cash/will-the-price-of-oil-reach-150-bef](https://manifold.markets/cash/will-the-price-of-oil-reach-150-bef) * [https://www.metaculus.com/questions/38768/](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/38768/) * [https://www.matteoiacoviello.com/gpr.htm](https://www.matteoiacoviello.com/gpr.htm)

comments.author: lubossaloky
comments.text:
My forecast is right-skewed. Maximum value for this index should have fat tail. Highs can be far above average.

Key sources of increased volatility:

1. Rates and bond-market (10-year near 5.2%)
2. Equity valuation and AI-related risk
3. November 3 midterms
4. Geopolitics (Israel election, Russia-EU, oil)
